[[File:Stole of the Amyrlin Seat.jpg|thumb|right|[[Tamra Ospenya]] wearing the Stole of the Amyrlin Seat]]

The '''Stole of the Amyrlin Seat''' is one of the symbolic items of regalia worn by the [[Amyrlin Seat]]. It is a long strip of silk, about "a hand wide" that the Amyrlin wears over her dress, that traditionally contains seven bands of color, one for each [[Ajah]]. Robert Jordan confirmed the order of these colors for the {{0}} graphic novel:{{ref|{{Link|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061026121036/http://www.silklantern.com/viewtopic.php?topic=10206&forum=7&43|text=Mystery of the Stole Unveiled}}}}
*[[Blue Ajah|Blue]]
*[[Green Ajah|Green]]
*[[Yellow Ajah|Yellow]]
*[[Red Ajah|Red]]
*[[White Ajah|White]]
*[[Gray Ajah|Gray]]
*[[Brown Ajah|Brown]]

These colors are also repeated on the hems of the dresses of [[Accepted]] in the [[White Tower]].

The size of the stole is a mystery. It is generally described as "broad,"{{ref/book|2|4}}{{ref/book|4|1}}{{ref/book|4|52}} in contrast to the "narrow" [[stole of the Keeper of the Chronicles]].{{ref/book|7|8}}{{ref/book|8|16}}{{ref/book|10|16}}{{ref/book|10|19}}{{ref/book|10|30}}{{ref/book|11|1}} [[Egwene al'Vere]] can store the stole in her belt pouch.{{ref/book|11|Prologue}} [[Elaida do Avriny a'Roihan]]'s stole is "wide enough to cover her shoulders."{{ref/book|11|25}} Perhaps, like the width of the Keeper's stole, the width of the Amyrlin's is based at least partly on personal preference.
[[File:Egwene in TAR.jpg|thumb|left|Egwene al'Vere in ''[[Tel'aran'rhiod]]'', by Liz Stepanoff]]

==Variants==
Just after the coup, Elaida is seen wearing the traditional seven-striped stole.{{ref/book|5|p}} However, she clearly resented the [[Blue Ajah]] and appeared in dreams wearing a six-striped stole with no blue stripe on three occasions.{{ref/book|5|15}}{{ref/book|6|7}}{{ref/book|7|32}} It is not clear when she made this a reality, but she is noted as wearing the six-striped version by [[Alviarin Freidhen]] on her return from [[Tremalking]]{{Ref/book|10|21}} and by [[Tarna Feir]] after Alviarin's replacement.{{ref/book|11|25}} Around the same time, the disbanding of the Blue Ajah was first mentioned.{{ref/book|10|16}} It's possible that the declaration of war by [[Egwene al'Vere]] in [[Murandy]] towards the end of [[The Path of Daggers]] was a precipitating event that caused such an irrevocable rift that Elaida could make her dreams a reality.{{ref/book|8|17}}

In contrast, Egwene and the rebel faction continued to represent all seven Ajahs by using the original seven-striped version, despite having no Red sisters supporting their cause. It is part of a running theme of Egwene pursuing unity and inclusion rather that Elaida's division and exclusion, and she potentially makes it a symbol of that difference.
